cohort: The study analyzed data from 31,615 neonates in Bahrain over five years, excluding stillbirths, abortions, and congenital anomalies discovered later in life.
finding: The prevalence of congenital anomalies was 1.1% (11.2 per 1000 births) and was significantly associated with nationality, method of conception, gender, method of delivery, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and gestational age at birth.
mod_finding: A statistically significant association was found between congenital anomalies and the method of delivery.
